thread:
Alex: heads up — noticed a bunch of provisional charges in the ledger that don't map to the route shown in the console. suspect canary router is changing mid-stream.
Nia: hmm, are these the toolcall+stream cases or plain streaming tokens?
Alex: toolcall inside a streaming session. pattern: client starts stream -> route r-canary -> toolcall TTL expires -> client reconnects -> routed to r-main -> final accounting attributes to r-main but provisional ledger entries were created under r-canary.
Sam: do we have session identifiers carrying route info? I thought session token was opaque.
Alex: right now session token is opaque blob from router; router adds `X-Route` header to backends but we don't persist that into the provisional ledger.
Kevin: logs? can you paste an example line?
Alex: sure — sanitized: `INFO stream_start sid=abc123 route=r-canary client=svc-a` then later `WARN toolcall_timeout sid=abc123 tool=fetch-prices ttl=15` then `INFO reconnect sid=def456 route=r-main client=svc-a` and ledger: `provisional charge sid=abc123 route=UNKNOWN tokens=42` then `confirmed charge sid=def456 route=r-main tokens=42`.
Nia: so the ledger loses the original route binding because on reconnect we mint a new sid.
Sam: does router generate a new sid on handoff? we used to preserve session ids when possible.
Kevin: canary uses sticky-less handoff to test routing weights; it intentionally drops affinity which causes a new sid.
Alex: that explains it. consequence: customer sees charges under main route, but provisional entries remain unclaimed and look like double charges until reconciliation runs.
Nia: immediate mitigation: tag provisional ledger entries with `orig_route` header when they're created (router injects it). then when reconnect/confirm happens we can stitch by `orig_route` + client id + timestamp window.
Sam: I like that. small change: we should also emit a telemetry field `billing_route` on stream events so console can surface which route the billing ledger used vs which route served responses. saves ops confusion.
Kevin: agree, but be careful with PII — client id is fine, but don't log request body.
Alex: simple header proposal for backend: `X-Redwood-Origin-Route: r-xxxx` and ledger write includes `origin_route` string.
Sam: UX ask: in the console Request detail pane show a small pill for "billing route" and a tooltip explaining provisional vs confirmed attribution. Ops can then filter by billing route when reconciling.
Nia: will need a migration for the provenance field in the provisional table — backfill heuristics?
Kevin: backfill by scanning recent provisional entries and matching previous `stream_start` logs. we can do best-effort for last 72h.
Alex: roadmap: 1) quick router header + ledger change (low risk), 2) emit telemetry metric `billing.route` in statsd, 3) console pill + filter, 4) backfill job for 72h.
Sam: estimate: 1 day for header+ledger change + tests, 2-3 days to wire metrics & console, backfill job 1 day.
Kevin: watch out for race: if provisional is written and then router restarts, origin header might be missing. add fallback `route=UNKNOWN` and make reconcile tolerant.
Alex: noted. I'll open a PR for the ledger patch and a tiny router change to add header when creating stream session.
deploy-bot: deploy queued for router/canary to prod-staging at 2024-06-18T15:22:00Z :rocket:
Nia: thanks — ping me on the PR, I can review the console bits.
Sam: also a thought — add a small alert when provisional_to_confirmed ratio > 0.2 for a route over 1h window. could catch regressions early.
Alex: good call. I'll add to the telemetry task.
Kevin: awesome. if no objections I'll tag this for the next eng-platform sprint. :thumbsup:
